sanskrit: etāvad uktvā śaineyo jalasaṃdhaṃ mahorasi vivyādha ṣaṣṭyā subhṛśaṃ śarāṇāṃ prahasann iva
english: Having spoken thus, the grandson of Śini pierced Jalasaṃdha full in his broad chest with sixty arrows, driving them home with force, as though laughing the while.

sanskrit: kṣurapreṇa ca pītena muṣṭideśe mahad dhanuḥ jalasaṃdhasya ciccheda vivyādha ca tribhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: And with a yellow razor-edged shaft he cut through Jalasaṃdha's great bow at the grip, and struck him with three more arrows.

sanskrit: jalasaṃdhas tu tat tyaktvā saśaraṃ vai śarāsanam tomaraṃ vyasṛjat tūrṇaṃ sātyakiṃ prati māriṣa
english: But Jalasaṃdha, casting aside that bow with its arrow, swiftly hurled a lance at Sātyaki, O honoured one.

sanskrit: sa nirbhidya bhujaṃ savyaṃ mādhavasya mahāraṇe abhyagād dharaṇīṃ ghoraḥ śvasann iva mahoragaḥ
english: Having pierced through the left arm of the Mādhava in that great battle, the dreadful weapon plunged into the earth, hissing like a mighty serpent.

sanskrit: nirbhinne tu bhuje savye sātyakiḥ satyavikramaḥ triṃśadbhir viśikhais tīkṣṇair jalasaṃdham atāḍayat
english: Though his left arm was pierced through, Sātyaki of true valour smote Jalasaṃdha with thirty sharp shafts.

sanskrit: pragṛhya tu tataḥ khaḍgaṃ jalasaṃdho mahābalaḥ ārṣabhaṃ carma ca mahac chatacandram alaṃkṛtam tata āvidhya taṃ khaḍgaṃ sātvatāyotsasarja ha
english: Then mighty Jalasaṃdha, seizing a sword and a great bull's-hide shield adorned with a hundred moons, and whirling that sword, flung it at the Sātvata.

sanskrit: śaineyasya dhanuś chittvā sa khaḍgo nyapatan mahīm alātacakravac caiva vyarocata mahīṃ gataḥ
english: That sword, having cut through the bow of the grandson of Śini, fell to the earth, and lying upon the ground it gleamed like a whirling circle of firebrand.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya sarvakāyāvadāraṇam śālaskandhapratīkāśam indrāśanisamasvanam visphārya vivyadhe kruddho jalasaṃdhaṃ śareṇa ha
english: Then, taking up another bow that could tear through any body, like the trunk of a śāla tree, twanging like Indra's thunderbolt, the wrathful one drew it and pierced Jalasaṃdha with an arrow.

sanskrit: tataḥ sābharaṇau bāhū kṣurābhyāṃ mādhavottamaḥ sāṅgadau jalasaṃdhasya ciccheda prahasann iva
english: Then with two razor-shafts the foremost of the Mādhavas, as though laughing, cut off both of Jalasaṃdha's arms, still bearing their ornaments and armlets.

sanskrit: tau bāhū parighaprakhyau petatur gajasattamāt vasuṃdharadharād bhraṣṭau pañcaśīrṣāv ivoragau
english: Those two arms, like iron bludgeons, fell from that finest of elephants, dropping from him who bore them earthward, like a pair of five-hooded serpents.

sanskrit: tataḥ sudaṃṣṭraṃ suhanu cārukuṇḍalam unnasam kṣureṇāsya tṛtīyena śiraś ciccheda sātyakiḥ
english: Then with a third razor-shaft Sātyaki severed his head, fine of tooth and jaw, with comely earrings and a lifted nose.

sanskrit: tat pātitaśirobāhukabandhaṃ bhīmadarśanam dviradaṃ jalasaṃdhasya rudhireṇābhyaṣiñcata
english: That headless, armless trunk, terrible to behold, drenched Jalasaṃdha's elephant with its blood.

sanskrit: jalasaṃdhaṃ nihatyājau tvaramāṇas tu sātvataḥ naiṣādiṃ pātayām āsa gajaskandhād viśāṃ pate
english: Having slain Jalasaṃdha in the fray, the Sātvata in haste struck down the Niṣāda prince too from the elephant's shoulders, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: rudhireṇāvasiktāṅgo jalasaṃdhasya kuñjaraḥ vilambamānam avahat saṃśliṣṭaṃ param āsanam
english: Jalasaṃdha's elephant, its limbs bathed in blood, bore upon it the splendid seat hanging askew and clinging fast to its back.

sanskrit: śarārditaḥ sātvatena mardamānaḥ svavāhinīm ghoram ārtasvaraṃ kṛtvā vidudrāva mahāgajaḥ
english: Tormented by the Sātvata's arrows, the great elephant, trampling its own ranks and uttering a dreadful cry of anguish, fled away.

sanskrit: hāhākāro mahān āsīt tava sainyasya māriṣa jalasaṃdhaṃ hataṃ dṛṣṭvā vṛṣṇīnām ṛṣabheṇa ha
english: A great cry of woe arose among your troops, O honoured one, when they saw Jalasaṃdha slain by that bull of the Vṛṣṇis.

sanskrit: vimukhāś cābhyadhāvanta tava yodhāḥ samantataḥ palāyane kṛtotsāhā nirutsāhā dviṣajjaye
english: Your warriors, turning their faces away, fled on every side, eager now for flight and without heart to vanquish the foe.

sanskrit: etasminn antare rājan droṇaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ abhyayāj javanair aśvair yuyudhānaṃ mahāratham
english: At that moment, O king, Droṇa, foremost of those who bear arms, advanced with swift horses upon Yuyudhāna, the great chariot-warrior.

sanskrit: tam udīrṇaṃ tathā dṛṣṭvā śaineyaṃ kurupuṃgavāḥ droṇenaiva saha kruddhāḥ sātyakiṃ paryavārayan
english: Seeing the grandson of Śini thus raging, the bulls of the Kurus, wrathful, together with Droṇa hemmed Sātyaki in on all sides.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ kurūṇāṃ sātvatasya ca droṇasya ca raṇe rājan ghoraṃ devāsuropamam
english: Then there broke out a battle between the Kurus and the Sātvata, and between Droṇa and him in that fray, O king — dreadful, like the war of gods and demons.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca te kirantaḥ śaravrātān sarve yattāḥ prahāriṇaḥ tvaramāṇā mahārāja yuyudhānam ayodhayan
english: Saṃjaya said: All those striking warriors, straining to the utmost and showering volleys of arrows, fought Yuyudhāna in haste, O great king.

sanskrit: taṃ droṇaḥ saptasaptatyā jaghāna niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ durmarṣaṇo dvādaśabhir duḥsaho daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Droṇa struck him with seventy-seven sharp arrows, Durmarṣaṇa with twelve, and Duḥsaha with ten shafts.

sanskrit: vikarṇaś cāpi niśitais triṃśadbhiḥ kaṅkapatribhiḥ vivyādha savye pārśve tu stanābhyām antare tathā
english: And Vikarṇa pierced him with thirty sharp heron-feathered arrows in the left flank, and in the space between his breasts.

sanskrit: durmukho daśabhir bāṇais tathā duḥśāsano 'ṣṭabhiḥ citrasenaś ca śaineyaṃ dvābhyāṃ vivyādha māriṣa
english: Durmukha struck the grandson of Śini with ten arrows, Duḥśāsana with eight, and Citrasena with two, O honoured one.

sanskrit: duryodhanaś ca mahatā śaravarṣeṇa mādhavam apīḍayad raṇe rājañ śūrāś cānye mahārathāḥ
english: And Duryodhana with a great rain of arrows beset the Mādhava in the battle, O king, as did other heroic great chariot-warriors.

sanskrit: sarvataḥ pratividdhas tu tava putrair mahārathaiḥ tān pratyavidhyac chaineyaḥ pṛthak pṛthag ajihmagaiḥ
english: Though pierced on every side by your sons, those great chariot-warriors, the grandson of Śini struck back at each of them severally with straight-flying shafts.

sanskrit: bhāradvājaṃ tribhir bāṇair duḥsahaṃ navabhis tathā vikarṇaṃ pañcaviṃśatyā citrasenaṃ ca saptabhiḥ
english: He struck the son of Bharadvāja with three arrows, Duḥsaha with nine, Vikarṇa with twenty-five, and Citrasena with seven.

sanskrit: durmarṣaṇaṃ dvādaśabhiś caturbhiś ca viviṃśatim satyavrataṃ ca navabhir vijayaṃ daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: He struck Durmarṣaṇa with twelve, Viviṃśati with four, Satyavrata with nine, and Vijaya with ten arrows.

sanskrit: tato rukmāṅgadaṃ cāpaṃ vidhunvāno mahārathaḥ abhyayāt sātyakis tūrṇaṃ putraṃ tava mahāratham
english: Then, brandishing his gold-banded bow, the great chariot-warrior Sātyaki swiftly advanced upon your son, that great chariot-warrior.

sanskrit: rājānaṃ sarvalokasya sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varam śarair abhyāhanad gāḍhaṃ tato yuddham abhūt tayoḥ
english: He smote with deep-driven arrows that king of all the world, that best of all who bear weapons; then there arose a battle between the two.

sanskrit: vimuñcantau śarāṃs tīkṣṇān saṃdadhānau ca sāyakān adṛśyaṃ samare 'nyonyaṃ cakratus tau mahārathau
english: Loosing sharp arrows and fitting fresh shafts to string, those two great chariot-warriors made each other invisible in the battle.

sanskrit: sātyakiḥ kururājena nirviddho bahv aśobhata asravad rudhiraṃ bhūri svarasaṃ candano yathā
english: Sātyaki, pierced deep by the king of the Kurus, shone resplendent, the blood flowing freely from him like sap from a sandal tree.

sanskrit: sātvatena ca bāṇaughair nirviddhas tanayas tava śātakumbhamayāpīḍo babhau yūpa ivocchritaḥ
english: And your son, pierced through by the floods of the Sātvata's arrows, gleamed like a tall sacrificial post crowned with a golden wreath.

sanskrit: mādhavas tu raṇe rājan kururājasya dhanvinaḥ dhanuś ciccheda sahasā kṣurapreṇa hasann iva athainaṃ chinnadhanvānaṃ śarair bahubhir ācinot
english: But the Mādhava in that fray, O king, swiftly cut through the bow of the Kuru king, that bowman, with a razor-shaft, as though laughing; and then, his bow severed, he covered him with many arrows.

sanskrit: nirbhinnaś ca śarais tena dviṣatā kṣiprakāriṇā nāmṛṣyata raṇe rājā śatror vijayalakṣaṇam
english: Pierced by the arrows of that swift-acting foe, the king could not endure in battle this mark of his enemy's triumph.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya hemapṛṣṭhaṃ durāsadam vivyādha sātyakiṃ tūrṇaṃ sāyakānāṃ śatena ha
english: Then, taking up another bow, gold-backed and hard to withstand, he swiftly pierced Sātyaki with a hundred shafts.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho balavatā putreṇa tava dhanvinā amarṣavaśam āpannas tava putram apīḍayat
english: Sorely pierced by your mighty son, that bowman, and overcome with fury, he beset your son in turn.

sanskrit: pīḍitaṃ nṛpatiṃ dṛṣṭvā tava putrā mahārathāḥ sātvataṃ śaravarṣeṇa chādayām āsur añjasā
english: Seeing the king hard pressed, your sons, those great chariot-warriors, at once covered the Sātvata with a rain of arrows.

sanskrit: sa chādyamāno bahubhis tava putrair mahārathaiḥ ekaikaṃ pañcabhir viddhvā punar vivyādha saptabhiḥ
english: Covered by your many sons, those great chariot-warriors, he pierced each of them with five arrows and then struck them again with seven.

sanskrit: duryodhanaṃ ca tvarito vivyādhāṣṭabhir āśugaiḥ prahasaṃś cāsya ciccheda kārmukaṃ ripubhīṣaṇam
english: And swiftly he pierced Duryodhana with eight fleet shafts, and laughing, he cut through his bow that struck terror in foes.

sanskrit: nāgaṃ maṇimayaṃ caiva śarair dhvajam apātayat hatvā tu caturo vāhāṃś caturbhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ sārathiṃ pātayām āsa kṣurapreṇa mahāyaśāḥ
english: With his arrows he brought down the jewelled serpent-banner, and slaying the four horses with four sharp shafts, the illustrious one struck down the charioteer with a razor-shaft.

sanskrit: etasminn antare caiva kururājaṃ mahāratham avākirac charair hṛṣṭo bahubhir marmabhedibhiḥ
english: And at that same moment, exulting, he overwhelmed the Kuru king, that great chariot-warrior, with many arrows that pierce the vital parts.

sanskrit: sa vadhyamānaḥ samare śaineyasya śarottamaiḥ prādravat sahasā rājan putro duryodhanas tava āplutaś ca tato yānaṃ citrasenasya dhanvinaḥ
english: Struck down in the fray by the finest arrows of the grandson of Śini, your son Duryodhana suddenly fled, O king, and leapt up into the chariot of Citrasena the bowman.

sanskrit: hāhābhūtaṃ jagac cāsīd dṛṣṭvā rājānam āhave grasyamānaṃ sātyakinā khe somam iva rāhuṇā
english: The whole world cried out in dismay to see the king in that battle being devoured by Sātyaki, as the moon in the sky is devoured by Rāhu.

sanskrit: taṃ tu śabdaṃ mahac chrutvā kṛtavarmā mahārathaḥ abhyayāt sahasā tatra yatrāste mādhavaḥ prabhuḥ
english: Hearing that great clamour, Kṛtavarman, the great chariot-warrior, rushed at once to the place where the lordly Mādhava stood.

sanskrit: vidhunvāno dhanuḥśreṣṭhaṃ codayaṃś caiva vājinaḥ bhartsayan sārathiṃ cograṃ yāhi yāhīti satvaraḥ
english: Brandishing his excellent bow, urging on his horses, and fiercely chiding his charioteer, he cried in haste, "On, on!"

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya vyāditāsyam ivāntakam yuyudhāno mahārāja yantāram idam abravīt
english: Beholding him bearing down like Death with gaping jaws, Yuyudhāna, O great king, spoke thus to his driver:

sanskrit: kṛtavarmā rathenaiṣa drutam āpatate śarī pratyudyāhi rathenainaṃ pravaraṃ sarvadhanvinām
english: "Kṛtavarman, armed with arrows, comes swiftly upon us in his chariot. Drive forward to meet him, this foremost of all bowmen."

sanskrit: tataḥ prajavitāśvena vidhivat kalpitena ca āsasāda raṇe bhojaṃ pratimānaṃ dhanuṣmatām
english: Then, with horses urged to full speed and his chariot duly arrayed, he closed in battle with the Bhoja, the very measure of all archers.

sanskrit: tataḥ paramasaṃkruddhau jvalantāv iva pāvakau sameyātāṃ naravyāghrau vyāghrāv iva tarasvinau
english: Then those two tigers among men, blazing in utmost wrath like two fires, came together like two swift and furious tigers.

sanskrit: kṛtavarmā tu śaineyaṃ ṣaḍviṃśatyā samārpayat niśitaiḥ sāyakais tīkṣṇair yantāraṃ cāsya saptabhiḥ
english: Kṛtavarman assailed the grandson of Śini with twenty-six sharp, keen shafts, and his charioteer with seven.

sanskrit: caturaś ca hayodārāṃś caturbhiḥ parameṣubhiḥ avidhyat sādhudāntān vai saindhavān sātvatasya ha
english: And with four excellent arrows he struck the four noble horses of the Sātvata, those well-trained steeds of the Sindhu breed.

sanskrit: rukmadhvajo rukmapṛṣṭhaṃ mahad visphārya kārmukam rukmāṅgadī rukmavarmā rukmapuṅkhān avākirat
english: He of the golden banner, the golden armlets, and the golden mail, twanging his great gold-backed bow, poured forth gold-feathered arrows.

sanskrit: tato 'śītiṃ śineḥ pautraḥ sāyakān kṛtavarmaṇe prāhiṇot tvarayā yukto draṣṭukāmo dhanaṃjayam
english: Then the grandson of Śini, intent and eager to behold Dhanaṃjaya, swiftly sped eighty shafts at Kṛtavarman.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho balavatā śatruṇā śatrutāpanaḥ samakampata durdharṣaḥ kṣitikampe yathācalaḥ
english: Sorely pierced by his mighty foe, that scorcher of foes, unassailable though he was, trembled as a mountain trembles in an earthquake.

sanskrit: triṣaṣṭyā caturo 'syāśvān saptabhiḥ sārathiṃ śaraiḥ vivyādha niśitais tūrṇaṃ sātyakiḥ kṛtavarmaṇaḥ
english: With sixty-three sharp arrows Sātyaki swiftly pierced Kṛtavarman's four horses, and his charioteer with seven.

sanskrit: suvarṇapuṅkhaṃ viśikhaṃ samādhāya sa sātyakiḥ vyasṛjat taṃ mahājvālaṃ saṃkruddham iva pannagam
english: Fitting a gold-feathered shaft to his bow, Sātyaki loosed it, blazing with great flame like an enraged serpent.

sanskrit: so 'viśat kṛtavarmāṇaṃ yamadaṇḍopamaḥ śaraḥ jāmbūnadavicitraṃ ca varma nirbhidya bhānumat abhyagād dharaṇīm ugro rudhireṇa samukṣitaḥ
english: That arrow, like the rod of Yama, entered Kṛtavarman, and piercing through his shining armour wrought of gold, it plunged fierce into the earth, drenched with blood.

sanskrit: saṃjātarudhiraś cājau sātvateṣubhir arditaḥ pracalan dhanur utsṛjya nyapatat syandanottame
english: Bleeding in the fray and tormented by the Sātvata's arrows, he reeled, and letting fall his bow, sank down upon his splendid chariot.

sanskrit: sa siṃhadaṃṣṭro jānubhyām āpanno 'mitavikramaḥ śarārditaḥ sātyakinā rathopasthe nararṣabhaḥ
english: That bull among men, lion-toothed and of measureless valour, tormented by Sātyaki's arrows, fell to his knees upon the floor of his chariot.

sanskrit: sahasrabāhoḥ sadṛśam akṣobhyam iva sāgaram nivārya kṛtavarmāṇaṃ sātyakiḥ prayayau tataḥ
english: Having checked Kṛtavarman — peer of the thousand-armed Arjuna, unshakable as the ocean — Sātyaki then passed onward.

sanskrit: khaḍgaśaktidhanuḥkīrṇāṃ gajāśvarathasaṃkulām pravartitograrudhirāṃ śataśaḥ kṣatriyarṣabhaiḥ
english: Strewn with swords, spears, and bows, thronged with elephants, horses, and chariots, made to flow with rivers of dread blood by hundreds of bulls among the warriors —

sanskrit: prekṣatāṃ sarvasainyānāṃ madhyena śinipuṃgavaḥ abhyagād vāhinīṃ bhittvā vṛtrahevāsurīṃ camūm
english: — through the midst of that host the bull of the Śinis broke, before the eyes of all the troops, cleaving the army as the slayer of Vṛtra cleaves the demon array.

sanskrit: samāśvāsya ca hārdikyo gṛhya cānyan mahad dhanuḥ tasthau tatraiva balavān vārayan yudhi pāṇḍavān
english: And the son of Hṛdika, having recovered himself and taken up another great bow, stood his ground there, mighty as he was, holding back the Pāṇḍavas in the fight.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca kālyamāneṣu sainyeṣu śaineyena tatas tataḥ bhāradvājaḥ śaravrātair mahadbhiḥ samavākirat
english: Saṃjaya said: As the troops were being driven hither and thither by the grandson of Śini, the son of Bharadvāja overwhelmed him with great showers of arrows.

sanskrit: sa saṃprahāras tumulo droṇasātvatayor abhūt paśyatāṃ sarvasainyānāṃ balivāsavayor iva
english: Tumultuous grew that combat between Droṇa and the Sātvata, before the eyes of all the troops, like the strife of Bali and Vāsava.

sanskrit: tato droṇaḥ śineḥ pautraṃ citraiḥ sarvāyasaiḥ śaraiḥ tribhir āśīviṣākārair lalāṭe samavidhyata
english: Then Droṇa pierced the grandson of Śini in the forehead with three bright all-iron arrows shaped like venomous snakes.

sanskrit: tair lalāṭārpitair bāṇair yuyudhānas tv ajihmagaiḥ vyarocata mahārāja triśṛṅga iva parvataḥ
english: With those straight-flying arrows fixed in his forehead, Yuyudhāna shone, O great king, like a three-peaked mountain.

sanskrit: tato 'sya bāṇān aparān indrāśanisamasvanān bhāradvājo 'ntaraprekṣī preṣayām āsa saṃyuge
english: Then the son of Bharadvāja, watching for his opening, sped at him still more arrows that rang like Indra's thunderbolt in the fray.

sanskrit: tān droṇacāpanirmuktān dāśārhaḥ patataḥ śarān dvābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ supuṅkhābhyāṃ ciccheda paramāstravit
english: Those arrows loosed from Droṇa's bow as they came flying, the Dāśārha, that master of supreme weapons, cut down two by two with well-feathered shafts.

sanskrit: tām asya laghutāṃ droṇaḥ samavekṣya viśāṃ pate prahasya sahasāvidhyad viṃśatyā śinipuṃgavam
english: Beholding that nimbleness of his, O lord of peoples, Droṇa laughed and suddenly pierced the bull of the Śinis with twenty arrows.

sanskrit: punaḥ pañcāśateṣūṇāṃ śatena ca samārpayat laghutāṃ yuyudhānasya lāghavena viśeṣayan
english: Again he assailed him with fifty arrows and then with a hundred, surpassing Yuyudhāna's nimbleness with his own swiftness of hand.

sanskrit: samutpatanti valmīkād yathā kruddhā mahoragāḥ tathā droṇarathād rājann utpatanti tanucchidaḥ
english: As angry great serpents dart up from an anthill, so, O king, did the body-cleaving shafts dart up from Droṇa's chariot.

sanskrit: tathaiva yuyudhānena sṛṣṭāḥ śatasahasraśaḥ avākiran droṇarathaṃ śarā rudhirabhojanāḥ
english: And in like manner the arrows loosed by Yuyudhāna in their hundreds and thousands, those blood-drinking shafts, rained down upon Droṇa's chariot.

sanskrit: lāghavād dvijamukhyasya sātvatasya ca māriṣa viśeṣaṃ nādhyagacchāma samāvāstāṃ nararṣabhau
english: Between the swiftness of hand of that foremost of brāhmaṇas and of the Sātvata, O honoured one, we could mark no difference: those two bulls among men were equal.

sanskrit: sātyakis tu tato droṇaṃ navabhir nataparvabhiḥ ājaghāna bhṛśaṃ kruddho dhvajaṃ ca niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ sārathiṃ ca śatenaiva bhāradvājasya paśyataḥ
english: Then Sātyaki, sorely wroth, smote Droṇa with nine smooth-jointed arrows, and his banner with sharp shafts, and his charioteer with a full hundred, while the son of Bharadvāja looked on.

sanskrit: lāghavaṃ yuyudhānasya dṛṣṭvā droṇo mahārathaḥ saptatyā sātyakiṃ viddhvā turagāṃś ca tribhis tribhiḥ dhvajam ekena vivyādha mādhavasya rathe sthitam
english: Seeing Yuyudhāna's swiftness of hand, Droṇa, the great chariot-warrior, pierced Sātyaki with seventy arrows, his horses with three apiece, and with a single shaft struck the banner standing on the Mādhava's chariot.

sanskrit: athāpareṇa bhallena hemapuṅkhena patriṇā dhanuś ciccheda samare mādhavasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Then with another gold-feathered, broad-headed winged shaft he cut through, in the battle, the bow of the high-souled Mādhava.

sanskrit: sātyakis tu tataḥ kruddho dhanus tyaktvā mahārathaḥ gadāṃ jagrāha mahatīṃ bhāradvājāya cākṣipat
english: Then Sātyaki, that great chariot-warrior, wroth, cast aside his bow, seized a mighty mace, and hurled it at the son of Bharadvāja.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ sahasā paṭṭabaddhām ayasmayīm nyavārayac charair droṇo bahubhir bahurūpibhiḥ
english: That iron mace bound about with cloth, as it came hurtling on, Droṇa warded off with many arrows of manifold forms.
